title: Check the Allergy First

patient.name: Mr Lim Cheng Hock
patient.presenting_complaint: Charted for an eye drop, but mentions he reacted badly to an eye drop before

history.hpc: Mr Lim says 'Last time one eye drop make my eye very red and swollen, I think I allergic.' He is charted for a drop today but cannot remember the exact name of the one he reacted to.
history.pmhx: Previous adverse reaction to an unspecified eye drop. Otherwise well.
history.allergies: No drug allergy recorded on file.
history.social_hx: Taxi driver; needs clear vision for work.

va.right: Not the focus of this station
va.left: Not the focus of this station

examination_findings.anterior_segment: No active infection that would change technique

investigations.task: Recognise and act on a reported eye-drop allergy before instilling — do not proceed until the allergy is clarified and the charted drop confirmed safe
investigations.key_points: Confirm identity; actively ask about and document the reported reaction; do not instil the charted drop until the allergy is clarified and the drop confirmed safe with the nurse/doctor; record the allergy

diagnosis: The key step is recognising and acting on a reported eye-drop allergy before instillation: the OA confirms identity, takes details of the previous reaction, withholds the charted drop, and checks with the nurse/doctor before proceeding. The allergy is documented. Patient safety is prioritised over completing the task. This is a procedural/safety station.

immediate: Confirm identity and the charted drop and strength
Actively ask about drug/eye-drop allergies and the details of the previous reaction
Do NOT instil the charted drop until the reported allergy is clarified
Check with the nurse/doctor whether the charted drop is safe or needs changing
Document the reported allergy clearly in the record
Only proceed with instillation once the drop is confirmed safe, using correct no-touch technique
Record the drop, eye, time and that allergy was checked
follow_up: Ensure the allergy is flagged in the patient's record to prevent future errors
Advise the patient to mention this allergy at every visit
patient_education: Reassure the patient that his reaction is taken seriously
Explain why the drop is being checked before use
Advise him to always report eye-drop reactions to staff
